study type: Retrospective medical record-based single center study
cohort: The study included 669 singleton live births in Vienna, Austria during the first COVID-19 lockdown phase (March-July 2020), compared with 277 live births during the pre-lockdown phase (January-February 2020) and 28,807 live births from 2005-2019.
finding: The stressful lockdown phase in Austria appeared to have no negative effect on gestational length and newborn weight among non-infected mothers; rather, mean birth weight was significantly higher and the rate of very low gestational age significantly lower during the lockdown phase.
birth_weight: Birth weight, low birth weight, very low birth weight, and extremely low birth weight were measured outcomes.
gest_age: Preterm birth, very low gestational age, and low gestational age were measured outcomes.
